input.strategy_title: Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag
input.strategy_markdown:
## Summary

RHOAI must provide a default vector store that is available out-of-the-box — without manual setup — so that Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag continue to function when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution image. Today these capabilities depend on an inline vector store provider bundled within the Llama Stack process; removing it (per RHAISTRAT-7474) will break them unless an alternative is available at the platform level.

## Problem Statement

Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag currently rely on an inline Milvus provider embedded in the Llama Stack distribution image to store and retrieve vector embeddings. This inline provider runs inside the Llama Stack process itself.

RHAISTRAT-7474 proposes removing inline providers from the Llama Stack distribution to improve GA readiness — shipping only what can be tested and maintained at scale, and aligning with Llama Stack's primary use case as a remote API server. However, no platform-level alternative exists today. If inline providers are removed without a replacement, any RHOAI user relying on Gen AI Studio's RAG capabilities or Auto Rag will lose functionality entirely — there is no workaround short of manually provisioning and configuring an external vector database.

Users expect vector storage to "just work" when they use Gen AI Studio or Auto Rag. The current out-of-the-box experience must be preserved even as the underlying architecture evolves.

## Affected Customers

* All RHOAI customers using Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
* All RHOAI customers using Auto Rag
* This is a platform-level product dependency: these features cannot function without a vector store

## Business Justification

* **Product integrity:** Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag are GA-track capabilities in RHOAI. Removing the inline vector store without a replacement breaks shipped product functionality for every user of these features.
* **Blocking dependency:** RHAISTRAT-7474 (removing inline providers for GA readiness) cannot proceed until this RFE is resolved. Silas Brenmark (Gen AI Studio lead) has identified this as a blocker.
* **User experience:** RHOAI differentiates on integrated, opinionated defaults. Requiring users to manually provision and configure a vector database before they can use the playground or Auto Rag degrades the out-of-the-box experience that customers expect from the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] A default vector store is available out-of-the-box on RHOAI without requiring users to manually provision or configure external infrastructure
* \[ \] Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] Auto Rag functions with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] The default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the Llama Stack instance (not an inline provider)
* \[ \] The default vector store is scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments (e.g., per-namespace isolation)
* \[ \] The default vector store is lightweight enough to run in resource-constrained environments without imposing significant overhead

## Success Criteria

* Users of Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag experience no functional regression when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution
* No additional manual setup steps are required for RAG workflows compared to the current experience
* RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and can proceed to implementation

## Open Questions

* What is the preferred scoping model — per namespace, per Llama Stack instance, or both? (Silas noted per-namespace is preferred for isolation, but Auto Rag may need per-instance scoping)
* Should users have a migration path from the default vector store to a production-grade vector database? (Bram Sundqvist raised the importance of aligning with commonly-used vector DB providers for easier migration)

## Strategy (AI Generated by Agentic SDLC Pipeline)

> **Note:** The full strategy exceeds Jira's description size limit and is stored as an attachment: `RHAISTRAT-8004-strategy.md`.

## Staff Engineer Input

**Correction 1 — OGX does not auto-provision PostgreSQL.** OGX defaults to SQLite for storage (`storage.kv.type: sqlite`, `storage.sql.type: sqlite` in the OGXServer CRD). The odh-dashboard gen-ai BFF hardcodes SQLite when creating OGXServer instances for the playground (`kv_sqlite` and `sql_sqlite` in `llamastack_config.go`). PostgreSQL is a supported backend but must be user-configured with an explicit `connectionString` secret. The strategy's claim that "every LlamaStackDistribution instance requires a PostgreSQL database" is incorrect — introducing PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension of existing infrastructure.

**Correction 2 — A Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector already exists.** The `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` image includes pgvector out of the box — confirmed in the [sclorg/postgresql-container Dockerfile](https://github.com/sclorg/postgresql-container/blob/master/16/Dockerfile.rhel9) (`INSTALL_PKGS="$INSTALL_PKGS pgvector"`). PostgreSQL 18 (RHEL 9) also includes pgvector. Furthermore, the model-registry-operator already uses `postgresql-16` as its auto-provisioned database image, and `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` is already present in the rhods-operator CSV for disconnected installs. No custom image build is needed. No Konflux onboarding is needed. The 1-2 sprint image onboarding estimate in the strategy can be eliminated.

**Architectural direction — platform-level database vs. self-provisioned.** Multiple RHOAI components now need PostgreSQL (model-registry, MLflow, and now OGX for pgvector). The preferred long-term direction is a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC, where each component consumes a connection string rather than self-provisioning. A shared platform-provided PostgreSQL via DSC will not be available until RHOAI 3.6. For 3.5, Gen AI Studio must provision its own PostgreSQL instance.

**Operator dependency for self-provisioning (RHAISTRAT-7164).** Self-provisioning PostgreSQL following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) would provide this operator layer. This is a hard dependency — until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers, there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. It will be challenging to commit this strategy to a specific release until that dependency is delivered.

**Fallback if RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time.** If the dashboard modularization is not ready for 3.5, the fallback is to require customers to bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Playground. Users would manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their PostgreSQL connection details. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the Playground largely abstracts OGX from users. The development team should define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of sprint planning.

**Decouple from Auto Rag.** Auto Rag integration with Gen AI Studio (RHAISTRAT-7824) is targeting RHOAI 3.6. This strategy should validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows. Auto Rag compatibility with pgvector will be addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824's scope. Remove Auto Rag from affected components, impacted teams, acceptance criteria, and validation requirements.

**Performance and index thresholds — dev experimentation scope.** The default pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation, not production usage. Strict latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) are not required. The sprint 1 benchmark should capture the inline Milvus baseline and verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude, not meet a specific threshold. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets — flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default. Users with production-scale vector workloads should use an external vector database. Remove open questions about latency thresholds, corpus size ranges, and index type selection.

**PostgreSQL resource sizing.** Reference the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource requests/limits as the starting point. Adjust based on sprint 1 benchmarking if needed.

**Alternative fallback — BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning.** If RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, an alternative to requiring customers to bring their own PostgreSQL is to have the gen-ai BFF provision the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails infrastructure. The BFF would create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured, if one does not already exist in the namespace. Caveats: (1) the implementation must be designed for portability — when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (3.6), the BFF should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning; (2) lifecycle management of the PostgreSQL instance must be carefully considered — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention.

**Existing remote vector store implementation is reusable.** Per the engineering team, the existing remote vector store implementation can be largely reused for pgvector integration. The majority of the work effort is around infrastructure and provisioning of the PostgreSQL/pgvector database, not the vector_io provider integration itself.

**Correction 3 — Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations.** The OGX vector_io provider configuration (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is completely separate from OGX's application storage backend configuration (`storage.kv.type`, `storage.sql.type`). This strategy only needs to configure the pgvector vector_io provider — it does not change the application storage backend, which remains on its existing default (SQLite). There is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because the application storage is not being touched. Remove any references to consolidating vector and application storage in a single database, and remove any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL upgrade path considerations.

# Operator-based PostgreSQL self-provisioning for the Gen AI Studio default vector store (branch A)

> **Conditional branch epic — outcome A of the provisioning go/no-go decision.** Selected
> only if the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) delivers the RHOAI-controlled
> operator layer in time for RHOAI 3.5. If a different outcome is selected, this epic does
> not exist.

## Description

This epic delivers the preferred provisioning outcome: PostgreSQL lifecycle management for
the Gen AI Studio default vector store implemented in the RHOAI-controlled operator layer
provided by the dashboard operator modularization, following the model-registry-operator's
established auto-provisioning pattern. When a Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
is configured, the operator provisions a dedicated PostgreSQL instance (with pgvector) in the
playground's namespace, and the remote pgvector vector_io provider configuration consumes
the provisioned connection string — giving users a default vector store that works
out-of-the-box with no manual setup.

The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry this RHOAI-specific provisioning logic;
that is why the RHOAI-controlled operator layer is a hard prerequisite for this branch.

## Scope

- Implement PostgreSQL self-provisioning in the RHOAI-controlled operator layer following the
  model-registry-operator pattern: per-namespace Deployment, Service and credential Secret
  created when a playground with RAG is configured, consumed via a connection string.
- Use the existing Red Hat `rhel9/postgresql-16` image, which includes pgvector out of the
  box — no custom image build and no build-pipeline onboarding work.
- Pin the database image for disconnected installs through the existing operator image
  reference mechanism (the PostgreSQL 16 related-image environment variable already present
  in the platform operator's CSV).
- Apply resource requests/limits to the provisioned PostgreSQL instance starting from the
  model-registry-operator's values, adjusted by the benchmark-derived sizing recommendation.
- Scope the instance per namespace (per-namespace isolation is the selected scoping model).
- Design for portability: when the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC
  becomes available (RHOAI 3.6+), the configuration consumes the shared connection string
  instead of self-provisioning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Configuring a Gen AI Studio playground with RAG causes a PostgreSQL instance (pgvector
  included) to be provisioned in the playground's namespace, with no manual user setup
  steps.
- The provisioned instance's credentials are delivered via a Secret and consumed by the
  remote pgvector vector_io provider configuration; playground RAG workflows (ingestion,
  embedding, retrieval) run end-to-end against the provisioned store.
- Deleting the playground configuration cleans up the provisioned PostgreSQL resources
  (garbage collection / finalization behaves correctly); pod restarts and credential
  handling are resilient.
- The database image is referenced through the operator's related-image mechanism so
  disconnected installs resolve to the pinned digest.
- The provisioned instance carries resource requests/limits derived from the
  model-registry-operator reference values and the benchmark sizing recommendation.
- The implementation demonstrably separates the provisioning point from the connection
  consumption point (a shared platform connection string can be substituted for
  self-provisioning without changing the consumer path).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — default vector store available out-of-the-box without manual
  provisioning: this epic is the delivery of that requirement under outcome A.
- **HLR-2 (P0)** — playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store:
  end-to-end acceptance criterion above.
- **HLR-5 (P0)** — multi-tenant scoping: per-namespace isolation of the provisioned
  instance.
- **HLR-6 (P0)** — lightweight operation: benchmark-derived resource sizing applied.

## Notes

- Hard prerequisite: the RHOAI-controlled operator layer from the dashboard operator
  modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) must be delivered; until then there is no
  RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live.
- Fallback if this outcome is not selected: BFF-managed provisioning (provisioning done
  directly by the gen-ai BFF) or bring-your-own PostgreSQL.

# BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning for the Gen AI Studio default vector store (branch B)

> **Conditional branch epic — outcome B of the provisioning go/no-go decision.** Selected
> only if the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) does not land in time for
> RHOAI 3.5 and the BFF-managed fallback is chosen over requiring customers to bring their
> own database. If a different outcome is selected, this epic does not exist.

## Description

This epic delivers the Staff Engineer's fallback provisioning outcome: the gen-ai BFF
provisions the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance for the playground directly — creating the
PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured and
no suitable instance exists in the namespace — following the pattern the BFF already uses
for guardrails infrastructure. This preserves the out-of-the-box experience without waiting
for the RHOAI-controlled operator layer.

Two caveats from the Staff Engineer shape the design work: **portability** (when the
platform-provided shared database becomes available in RHOAI 3.6+, the BFF must consume the
shared connection string rather than self-provisioning) and **lifecycle management** (the
BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion,
handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention).

## Scope

- Implement BFF-managed provisioning of the default PostgreSQL instance (existing Red Hat
  `rhel9/postgresql-16` image, pgvector included — no custom image build): Deployment,
  Service, PVC and credential Secret created in the playground's namespace when RAG is
  configured and no instance exists, with the remote pgvector vector_io provider
  configuration consuming the provisioned connection string.
- Design and implement lifecycle handling appropriate for a non-reconciling provisioner:
  cleanup on playground deletion, recovery from PostgreSQL pod restarts, and a credential
  rotation approach — each documented as an explicit design decision.
- Scope the instance per namespace (per-namespace isolation is the selected scoping model).
- Apply resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL
  values, adjusted by the benchmark-derived sizing recommendation.
- Structure the provisioning behind a portability seam: the connection source (self-provided
  vs. platform-provided shared connection string) is a swappable configuration decision, so
  the 3.6 shared-database consumption path requires no rework of the consumer side.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Configuring a Gen AI Studio playground with RAG causes the BFF to provision a
  PostgreSQL instance (pgvector included) in the playground's namespace when none exists,
  with no manual user setup steps.
- Playground RAG workflows (ingestion, embedding, retrieval) run end-to-end against the
  BFF-provisioned store via the remote pgvector provider configuration.
- Deleting the playground configuration cleans up the provisioned PostgreSQL resources
  (Deployment, Service, PVC, Secret) — documented and demonstrated; pod restarts of the
  PostgreSQL instance do not break subsequent RAG workflows; credential rotation is
  designed and implemented.
- The provisioned instance carries resource requests/limits derived from the
  model-registry-operator reference values and the benchmark sizing recommendation.
- The connection source is demonstrably swappable: supplying an external/shared connection
  string in place of self-provisioning requires configuration only, not code changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — default vector store available out-of-the-box without manual
  provisioning: this epic is the delivery of that requirement under outcome B.
- **HLR-2 (P0)** — playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store:
  end-to-end acceptance criterion above.
- **HLR-5 (P0)** — multi-tenant scoping: per-namespace isolation of the provisioned
  instance.
- **HLR-6 (P0)** — lightweight operation: benchmark-derived resource sizing applied.

## Notes

- Fallback relationships: this branch exists only if the operator-based outcome is not
  selected; if BFF-managed provisioning is also ruled out, the residual path is
  bring-your-own PostgreSQL.

# Bring-your-own PostgreSQL support for Gen AI Studio RAG (branch C)

> **Conditional branch epic — outcome C of the provisioning go/no-go decision.** Selected
> only if neither self-provisioning path (operator-based or BFF-managed) lands for RHOAI
> 3.5. This is the explicitly degraded fallback: it does **not** satisfy the out-of-the-box
> requirement — customers must supply their own PostgreSQL. If a different outcome is
> selected, this epic does not exist.

## Description

This epic delivers the residual fallback outcome directed by the Staff Engineer Input:
customers bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the playground. Users manually
configure the OGXServer custom resource spec with their PostgreSQL connection details, and
the remote pgvector vector_io provider configuration consumes them. This aligns with the
breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the playground otherwise largely
abstracts OGX from users. The epic is small by design: the provider wiring already works
with any supplied pgvector endpoint; what remains is ensuring the user-provided
configuration path is supported, does not fight the playground's defaults, and is
documented.

## Scope

- Ensure the user-provided PostgreSQL configuration path works: an OGXServer instance whose
  spec carries customer-supplied PostgreSQL connection details (via Secret reference) runs
  playground RAG workflows against that database through the remote pgvector vector_io
  provider configuration.
- Ensure the playground's OGXServer-instance handling does not override or break
  user-supplied database configuration (the configuration surface treats a supplied

# Configure the remote pgvector vector_io provider for Gen AI Studio OGXServer instances

## Description

This epic delivers the vector-store-side wiring that is common to **every** provisioning
outcome: configuring the OGX instances created for the Gen AI Studio playground to use the
remote pgvector vector_io provider (`remote::pgvector`, activated via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`)
instead of the removed inline Milvus provider. The existing remote vector store
implementation is largely reusable — per the engineering team, the provider integration is
the small part of this strategy's effort — so this epic is configuration and wiring work in
the gen-ai BFF's OGXServer-instance creation path, not new provider development in the OGX
distribution.

This work is deliberately decoupled from, and runs in parallel with, the provisioning
approach decision: whichever outcome is selected (operator-based self-provisioning,
BFF-managed provisioning, or bring-your-own PostgreSQL), the OGX vector I/O configuration is
the same — only the source of the PostgreSQL connection string differs.

## Scope

- Enable the remote pgvector vector_io provider on OGXServer instances created for the Gen
  AI Studio playground (activation via the `ENABLE_PGVECTOR` environment guard, following the
  distribution's conditional provider-activation pattern).
- Inject the PostgreSQL connection details (host, port, database, credentials) through the
  existing secret-resolution mechanism (Secret-backed environment variables), so the same
  wiring works whether the database is provisioned by the operator layer, by the BFF, or
  supplied by the user.
- Keep OGX **application storage** untouched: `storage.kv.type` and `storage.sql.type` remain
  on their existing SQLite default. Vector storage and application storage are independent
  configurations; there is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern in this epic.
- Preserve the escape hatch: the vector store configuration can be pointed at an external,
  user-managed vector database instead of the default pgvector instance (users with
  production-scale vector workloads are directed to an external database).

## Acceptance Criteria

- An OGXServer instance created for a Gen AI Studio playground activates the remote
  pgvector vector_io provider, and the provider connects successfully to a PostgreSQL
  instance with pgvector available when its connection details are supplied.
- Connection credentials are read from a Kubernetes Secret via the distribution's
  secret-resolution mechanism — no database credentials appear in plaintext in the
  OGXServer spec, ConfigMap or logs.
- The OGX application storage backend remains on its existing default (SQLite) — verified
  unchanged by this configuration work.
- Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows (document ingestion, embedding, retrieval) complete
  successfully against a pgvector-backed vector store with no loss of the current inline
  Milvus capability, when a reachable pgvector endpoint is supplied.
- Pointing the configuration at an external vector database (connection details swapped)
  is demonstrated to work — the default is an opinionated default, not a lock-in.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector
  store with no loss of current capability: this epic is the provider wiring that makes the
  playground talk to pgvector.
- **HLR-4 (P0)** — the default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the
  OGX instance: the remote `remote::pgvector` provider configuration is exactly this
  decoupling; no inline provider is used.

## Notes

- Strategy open questions on latency thresholds, corpus size and index type are resolved by
  the Staff Engineer Input as out of scope: the default store targets development
  experimentation, flat scan (no index) is sufficient, and performance is verified by the
  benchmark workstream (order-of-magnitude parity with the inline Milvus baseline), not by
  SLAs.
